statements.venue: Op-ed on his own Substack newsletter, Into the Weeds ("Tie Them to the Mast")
statements.quote: But we may well face the moment of gravest danger in AI’s development in a matter of months, not years, and many experts’ p(doom) exceeds my own p(Congress and this president agreeing quickly on AI regulation with real teeth).
statements.context: Arguing that Congress must regulate AI and that, until it does, state attorneys general should use multistate investigations to impose enforceable safety requirements on all major AI companies.
statements.source_label: Into the Weeds by Micah Lasher (Substack)
statements.reason: Says in his own words that AI's moment of gravest danger may be months away and invokes experts' probability of doom; catastrophic risk from AI itself, between A and B because extinction or permanent loss of control is implied rather than stated.

statements.venue: Campaign website, Platform and Policies page (undated; date given is the date it was read)
statements.quote: Cooperate with partners and experts across the globe to minimize artificial general intelligence- and superintelligence-related risks, including through potential binding international treaties.
statements.context: One of his pledges for Congress under the campaign's AI platform section, alongside a national data center moratorium and protections against AI mass surveillance.
statements.reason: Acknowledges risks from artificial general intelligence and superintelligence in general terms without naming a catastrophic harm.

slowdown.note: No explicit call to slow frontier AI for safety. His platform backs a national data center moratorium, but tied to environment and costs, which does not count. His op-ed favors enforceable 'restrictions' and 'guardrails' and says U.S. guardrails 'need not set us back' against China.

pause.note: No statement found on a pause of frontier AI development.

intl.note: Platform pledges 'potential binding international treaties' on AGI and superintelligence risks with 'partners and experts across the globe', but does not mention China or pacing; the op-ed's China discussion is about export controls and pressure on Beijing, not an agreement. Reviewer may consider 'mixed'.

rsi.note: No statement found on banning self-improving AI.

record: Co-sponsor in the New York State Assembly of A6453, the RAISE Act on safety of frontier AI models (sponsor Alex Bores); passed in substituted Senate form and was signed into law on 19 December 2025.

grade_reason: His 5 October 2026 op-ed says in his own words that AI's 'moment of gravest danger' may be months away and that AI development carries 'risks to civilization', a catastrophic risk not limited to misuse. Nothing dismissive was found.
notes: Eight web searches ran; none were refused. Micah Lasher (NY Assembly District 69, Manhattan) won the NY-12 primary against Alex Bores in a race with heavy AI-industry spending. The op-ed was read in full at its source (downloaded page text). The campaign platform page blocked direct download (Cloudflare); its wording was obtained through a page-fetch tool that returned the passage in two consecutive chunks, so exact spacing should be checked by a reviewer; the page has no date, so the date is the date read. The op-ed also relays others' warnings: CEOs believe guardrails are needed so products 'don’t do vast damage', and quotes Florida's Attorney General on 'potentially civilization-ending endeavors' (not his words, so not quoted). He mentions tools 'that may take on lives of their own'. News reports (Route Fifty, WTOP, Fox News, City & State) describe him as a supporter of AI regulation and say he pointed to his record standing up to Big Tech; I did not find direct quotes from him on catastrophic risk there. A webpronews article could not be opened (403). No evidence found of sponsoring the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act. Consider whether 'risks to civilization' plus 'p(doom)' should be A under ruling 1; I chose B with boundary.
